Q: How to average multiple files across groups A:

I had a go at making some mock data to make it reproducible. Let me know if it fails to reflect your data sufficiently.

Set up example data

# making some names and groups. group sizes are 3, 3 and 2

fnames <- head(paste0("samp_", outer(letters[1:3], 1:3, paste0), ".csv"), -1)
fileid <- do.call("rbind", strsplit(substr(fnames, 6, 7), ""))

# the reference file for making the group averages

meangroups <- data.frame(
  group=fileid[,1], 
  file=fnames, 
  outname=paste(
    "meangroup",
    fileid[,1],
    apply(fileid, 1, 
      function(x) paste(fileid[fileid[,1] == x[1], 2], collapse="-")),
    sep="_"
  )
)
write.csv(meangroups, file="meangroups.csv")

# creating a subdirectory with some randomly generated files, 
# using the predefined names

dir.create("subf")
set.seed(1)
for (i in seq_along(fnames)) {
    write.csv(matrix(sample(0:9, 12, rep=TRUE), nrow=4), 
      file=paste0("subf/", fnames[i]))
}

# remove the recently made objects, we shouldn't need them

rm("fnames", "fileid", "meangroups")

Read in example data and compute group averages

# read in reference file

scang <- read.csv("meangroups.csv", row.names=1)

# read in data files, compute group averages, and write averaged data to 
# appropriately named files.
# i think group_by() works similarly to split() here. we could have used
# tapply() instead of lapply(split()), but this makes it a bit more clear 
# what's going on, i think

lapply(split(scang, scang[,1]), 
  function(x) {
      l <- lapply(paste0("subf/", x[,2]), read.csv, row.names=1)
      l.mean <- Reduce("+", l)/length(l)
      write.csv(l.mean, file=paste0(x[1,3], ".csv"))
  })

# chack that it worked

lapply(paste0(unique(scang[,3]), ".csv"), read.csv, row.names=1)

# [[1]]
#         V1       V2       V3
# 1 4.666667 5.666667 4.666667
# 2 4.000000 6.000000 3.666667
# 3 6.333333 4.666667 5.000000
# 4 2.333333 3.000000 9.000000

# [[2]]
#         V1       V2       V3
# 1 5.333333 3.000000 5.000000
# 2 6.000000 6.000000 5.000000
# 3 2.666667 5.666667 4.000000
# 4 6.000000 5.666667 7.333333

# [[3]]
#    V1  V2  V3
# 1 6.5 4.0 4.5
# 2 3.5 8.0 3.0
# 3 4.5 8.5 7.5
# 4 1.0 6.5 6.5

Q: Real-time text-to-speech with Deepgram on React Native A:

You can use nobodywho inference engine : https://github.com/nobodywho-ooo/nobodywho

Here is the package on npm. It supports STT with Whisper and TTS with Supertonic/PocketTTS/Kokoro.

For STT, you can use transcribeFile (e.g an mp3 file) or directly from a buffer with transcribePcm.

Q: What are the differences between APT clean, remove, purge, etc. commands? A:

Basically, remove uninstalls a package, purge also removes its config files, autoremove removes unused dependencies, and clean clears APT's downloaded package cache. You usually don't need to run all of them together.

Q: avoid string printed to console getting truncated (in RStudio) A:

I'm using Rstudio R4.5.1 and managed to find the solution under Tools > Global Options > Console > Truncate lines to maximum length (characters).

Q: Apache Camel - Backbone of IT infrastructure? A:

Apache Camel can be a strong choice for integrating services, but I would be careful about making it the entire backbone of an IT infrastructure. It is primarily an integration framework, so separating integration responsibilities from core infrastructure can make the architecture easier to manage. For larger environments, IT infrastructure solutions should be designed with appropriate routing, redundancy, and monitoring. Well-planned Enterprise IT solutions can also provide the flexibility needed to support Scalable IT infrastructure as workloads grow.

Q: AWS Lambda@Edge not logging A:

I had the same issue : lambda was running fine in Test mode, but when calling it from the browser there were no log created.

Permission were fine : CreateLogGroup etc allowed for * but no log written.

It was because my company had a policy to prevent usage of un-approved region, and the lambda was not able to create logs in an un approved region (but the lambda was working fine, only no logs generated).

To highlight this :

  • run a "curl --verbose" command to highlight the "X-Amz-Cf-Pop" and find the correct region associated to this PoP (for ex : CDG is eu-west-3, DUB is eu-west-1). Eventually, use CloudShell to trigger the curl from different location

  • check for CloudWatch Logs in the PoP region

  • if no log created for the PoP region, try to manually create the logs stream in the AWS console

  • if you got an error saying "is not authorized to perform: logs:CreateLogGroup on resource: arn:aws:logs:xxx:xxx:log-group:xxx with an explicit deny in a service control policy: arn:aws:organizations::xxx:policy/o-xxx/service_control_policy/p-xxx" it means you have a control policy preventing log creation

Q: Configure VS Code `Enter` as newline, not send Copilot Chat prompt A:

Use the Keyboard Shortcuts menu item Open Keyboard Shortcuts (JSON) and delete the default Enter submit binding; then add Enter binding to the type command with "\n". This will cause Enter to add a new line, and Ctrl+Enter to send the prompt.

Q: I can't remove python pip A:

If you are a Windows user, make sure you run 'python -m pip uninstall pip' in administrator mode.

Q: How to uninstall a package installed with pip install --user A:

I am running Anaconda version 4.3.22 and a Python 3.6.1 environment, and I had this problem. Here's the history and the fix:

pip uninstall opencv-python # The original step. It failed.

Error:

ImportError: DLL load failed: The specified module could not be found.

I did this into my Python 3.6 environment and got this error.

python -m pip install opencv-python # The same package as above.
conda install -c conda-forge opencv # A separate install parallel to OpenCV
pip-install opencv-contrib-python # As suggested by another user here. It doesn't resolve it.

Next, I tried downloading Python 3.6 and putting the python3.dll file in the folder and in various folders. Nothing changed.

Finally, this fixed it:

pip uninstall opencv-python

(The other Conda Forge version is still installed.) This left only the Conda version, and that works in Python 3.6.

import cv2

is working (interactively)!
